transcript:
Doctor: Ms. Delacroix, you're here about your knee. Tell me what's going on.
Patient: My right knee has been killing me for the past six months. It's worse in the morning when I first get up, and after I sit for a long time. The stiffness lasts maybe 20 minutes in the morning then gets better.
Doctor: Any swelling, clicking, or locking?
Patient: Some swelling after I walk a lot. No locking. There's a crunchy feeling when I bend it.
Doctor: Any trauma or injury?
Patient: No. I'm 58 years old, I've been overweight most of my life. My mother had the same problem.
Doctor: On exam, BMI is 32. I see mild periarticular swelling of the right knee. Range of motion is 5 to 110 degrees with pain at end range. Crepitus on passive flexion. No ligamentous laxity. Medial joint line tenderness on palpation. X-ray shows moderate joint space narrowing medially, osteophyte formation, and subchondral sclerosis — classic osteoarthritis.
Patient: Is there anything that helps besides surgery?
Doctor: Yes, several things. First I'm going to start you on naproxen 500mg twice daily with food for anti-inflammatory effect. Take it consistently for two to four weeks. Also, I want you in physical therapy to strengthen the quadriceps — that takes pressure off the joint. Weight loss will significantly help as well.
Patient: What about those injections I read about?
Doctor: Corticosteroid injections are an option if the naproxen doesn't give enough relief. We can discuss that at follow-up in six weeks. I'd also recommend you start acetaminophen 500mg every 6 hours as needed on days when the naproxen isn't enough, but don't exceed 3 grams per day.
Patient: Okay. What about supplements like glucosamine?
Doctor: The evidence is mixed. I don't routinely recommend it, but it won't hurt if you want to try it. Focus on the PT and weight loss — those have the best evidence.
Patient: And if nothing works?
Doctor: Total knee replacement is very effective for moderate to severe osteoarthritis when conservative measures fail. But we're not there yet.
